title: Terse reviewer output
description: When aiadev.terseMode is on, reviewer subagents (spec-document-reviewer, plan-document-reviewer, code-reviewer) must emit findings in this shape. One finding = one line. Multi-paragraph messages are rejected so the 30% token-reduction target (spec 0009) remains measurable. As of spec 0014 Story 3 sc5, an APPROVED verdict's `### Why no issues` block is encoded as 🟢 findings with `kind: "verification"` — one per audit check, rendered as `🟢 file:line — verificação realizada`.

verdict.description: The reviewer's top-line decision. Mirrors the existing non-terse verdict vocabulary.

findings.description: Zero or more one-line findings. APPROVED verdict typically has an empty list.

severity.description: Glyph prefix. Red = blocking, yellow = should-fix, green = nit/FYI or verification (see `kind`).

location.description: Non-whitespace pointer: typically `file:line` but plan-reviewer findings use `file:TASK` (e.g. `tasks.md:T015`). The regex enforces only the no-whitespace invariant; semantic shape is documented here.

message.description: Single-line finding. No newlines. 140-char ceiling keeps lines terminal-friendly and keeps the token-reduction target honest.

kind.description: Optional discriminator for 🟢 findings. `nit` (default when omitted) is an FYI; `verification` is an explicit audit check listed under APPROVED's `### Why no issues` block — Story 3 sc5 of spec 0014. Reviewer subagents emit one such finding per check (e.g. `🟢 file:line — verificação realizada`).

then.$comment: verification findings are intrinsically green: they record a passing audit, not a defect.
